reason: The text contains two primary named individual characters: Moses (מֹשֶׁה) and Pharaoh (פַּרְעֹה). Neither qualifies as a 'regular person.' Moses is explicitly established as a prophet who receives direct divine instructions and performs miracles (dividing the sea). Pharaoh is the monarch and supreme ruler of Egypt. Both are extraordinary figures with exceptional authority and roles—Moses operating as God's agent, Pharaoh wielding absolute political power. The collective entities (Israelites, Egyptians) are group references rather than individual named characters.
